BELAVADÖS
CORRECTED SPATIAL, GEOLOGICAL, AND WEATHER INDEX
Final province centers • all 280 settlement and territory anchors • biome/depth matches • climate correction

All province and settlement placement in this index comes from the edited biome-remapped document and its final embedded GeoJSON. Longitude and latitude use the 2048 × 1024 equirectangular surface map. Mapped biome/depth and match status come from the final coordinate directories. Canonical non-spatial values remain unchanged. Climate descriptions are recalculated from corrected latitude ranges, canonical biomes, final mapped terrain/depth, and preserved named weather and vertical records.
UTC offset = clamp(floor((longitude + 7.5) / 15), -12, +12). Earth-reference locations remain confined to the source document’s final appendix and are not used as Belavadös names.

The edited spatial source records 596 renamed natural-system objects: 126 province-based and 470 settlement-based. Their source categories and coordinate anchors remain fixed; the full corrected map layers and placement plates are reproduced in the complete spatial register appended to the final geology and weather compendium.

A world-specific conversion of the Earth deep-interior-to-exosphere guide into the current Belavadös topography base
Figure 1. The full Belavadös layer stack from inner core to exosphere.

This DOCX converts the Earth Deep-to-Space 3D Map Simulation Guide into Belavadös canon. It preserves the Earth-sized physical model for the deep interior, crust, atmosphere, and exosphere, but replaces Earth surface data with the current Belavadös topography base: the shared full-world height map, biome categories, vertical bands, province centers, settlement pin anchors, named waters, deep places, and map render rules.

The goal is a usable 3D view specification from the absolute inside to the absolute outside: inner core, outer core, mantle, lithosphere, terrain shell, water column, caverns, settlement anchors, weather, atmosphere, aurora/ionosphere, exosphere, moons, and starfield.

3. Absolute inside: core, mantle, lithosphere, and crust

The inside of Belavadös should use the same Earth-scale structural layer model unless a later world-canon document explicitly changes the planet physics. The inner core and outer core are not terrain meshes; they are cutaway objects, heat/magnetic drivers, and deep-lore layers. The mantle is the tectonic engine. The lithosphere/crust is the rigid shell where the actual Belavadös terrain, caverns, ocean floors, and settlement anchors live.
Figure 3. Cutaway shell view showing the interior and the outer render shells.

blocks.text: The Belavadös terrain shell is not a flat texture. It is a signed elevation and depth system: land is positive z, ocean/cavern/seafloor is negative z, and ocean-surface infrastructure can display at z=0 while still carrying bathymetry beneath it. The topography base uses 17 biome categories and 8 vertical bands.
Figure 4. Current biome-category share across the classified world raster.
Figure 5. Current vertical-band share across the world raster.

The region-key ledger is the compact form of the current world surface. Each row is a modeled combination of biome and vertical band. In runtime, the renderer can use this key to choose material, water behavior, pressure, vegetation, slope treatment, collision, weather, and settlement anchor logic.

blocks.text: A side view of Belavadös should show a continuous solid planet section. Mountains have roots and slopes. Coasts continue into shallows before a major drop unless they are fjords, volcanic islands, active fault coasts, or trench-adjacent margins. Deep-sea and cavern settlements need ledges, basin floors, canyon walls, reef rims, vent fields, tunnels, shafts, or engineered anchor structures.
Figure 6. Belavadös profile using the current canonical vertical range.
Mountains: build connected ridges, passes, talus, ravines, foothills, and drainage instead of isolated spikes.
Coasts: stage the transition through beaches, marshes, estuaries, reef flats, shelves, shelf breaks, slopes, rises, abyssal plains, and trench walls.
Caverns: model true subsurface volumes with ceilings, floors, shafts, ramps, under-roads, aquifers, and solid rock around them.
Water: render a separate water shell and separate seafloor/bathymetry mesh; never let ocean be only a color layer.
Pins: keep surfaceAnchor, subsurfaceAnchor, and displayZ separate so underwater, cavern, mountain-side, and floating settlements behave correctly.

blocks.text: 9. Atmosphere, sky, moons, and absolute outside

Belavadös keeps the Earth-like atmosphere layer sequence for simulation behavior: troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere/ionosphere, and exosphere. Use ranges rather than hard walls. The atmosphere belongs to the same globe system as terrain: mountains drive cloud lift, seas drive humidity and storms, trenches drive deep fog and cold upwelling, and named weather marks repeated geomorphic processes.
Figure 8. Render shells for terrain, water, sky scattering, aurora, and exosphere.

blocks.text: 8. Geography, Water, Weather, and Vertical Law

Belavadös is a wet, broken, living map: broad green continents cut by inland seas, drowned shelves, reef lace, island chains, high storm mountains, trench roads, and forested coasts. Every blue expanse is road, food source, divine depth, weather engine, monster habitat, and legal border.

blocks.text: The deep cold of Belavadös is not a white lid over the world. It is a hidden under-architecture. The abyss holds blue-black ice-crowns, hydrate stone, cold brine lakes, mineral chimneys, sleeping eggs, pressure-slow microbes, and god-sealed vaults.

When trench walls crack or deep currents lift fragments, an omenberg can appear far from any place that feels cold enough to make ice. Such bergs can carry freshwater, poison, old bones, living spores, alchemical salts, or the sound of the pressure shelf that birthed them.
